title: [Illustrative] TREM2 agonism helps only once plaques are established
statement: TREM2 agonism has no effect on neuritic dystrophy at an early stage and reduces it at a late stage, in brains with functional TREM2.
mechanism: Early plaques are already compacted by baseline TREM2 signalling, so extra agonism adds nothing; late, signalling is saturated by soluble TREM2 and agonism restores it.
predictions: Early stage, TREM2-normal: no change vs vehicle.
Late stage, TREM2-normal: agonist reduces dystrophy vs vehicle.

experiments.design: Amyloid-positive mouse model, TREM2-normal and TREM2 loss-of-function arms, early and late stage, agonist antibody vs vehicle.
experiments.readout: Neuritic dystrophy (LAMP1+ dystrophic neurites per plaque) relative to vehicle.

evidence.note: Illustrative demo hypothesis. No literature was consulted and none is claimed; the formal check never reads this field.

focus_area: Illustrative Stage 1 target: TREM2 agonism in amyloid pathology (CoResearcher OASE adapter demo)
